compatibility.title: Which Alfa Romeo Models Use the 55273835 2.0 GME?
compatibility.intro: The 55273835 is the Alfa Romeo-specific variant of the FCA Global Medium Engine (GME) family. Developed under the "Giorgio" code project for Alfa Romeo's rear‑biased platforms, it is used exclusively in Alfa Romeo models, covering both the Giulia saloon and the Stelvio SUV in rear‑wheel drive and Q4 all‑wheel drive configurations. The engine has been in production since 2016 and is available in multiple states of tune.

costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a 55273835 2.0 GME typically takes 10-14 hours at £80-£120/hr (independent Alfa Romeo specialist) - the transverse/longitudinal layout and MultiAir system add complexity, and the Giorgio platform's aluminium-intensive construction requires specialist knowledge.【PATTERN DATA】
paragraphs: The biggest price movers for a 55273835 replacement are timing chain condition (stretch can occur as early as 40,000 miles), MultiAir system health, turbocharger condition, and whether the engine is a 200 hp or 280 hp variant - higher‑output units may command a premium. failures.title: Alfa Romeo 55273835 2.0 GME Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Timing Chain Stretch - the most critical wear item
items.whatHappens: The 2.0 GME engine can develop timing chain elongation as early as 40,000 miles, causing cold‑start rattle, rough idle, and Check Engine warnings for camshaft correlation faults. Left unaddressed, the chain can skip teeth and cause catastrophic valve‑to‑piston contact. The issue appears to be linked to oil quality and change intervals - 2020+ models have fewer reported instances.
items.repairVsReplace: Timing chain and tensioner replacement costs £1,500-£3,000 at a specialist. If the chain has skipped and bent valves, a full replacement engine is required. Read our full /failures/timing-chain-failure guide

items.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves - the GDi penalty
items.whatHappens: Like all direct‑injection petrol engines, the GME's fuel injectors spray directly into the combustion chamber, bypassing the intake valves. This means there is no fuel washing the intake valves clean, allowing carbon deposits to accumulate. Symptoms include misfires, rough idle, reduced power, and in severe cases, ignition coil damage from prolonged misfires.
items.repairVsReplace: Walnut‑blasting service is required every 30,000-50,000 miles to restore airflow - costs £400-£800. Preventative: occasional Italian tune‑ups and high‑quality fuel can help reduce carbon accumulation. Read our full /failures/carbon-buildup guide

items.title: Fuel Pump and Fuel Delivery Module Failure
items.whatHappens: A significant recall affecting Giulia and Stelvio models involves the fuel delivery module (FDM), whose internal components are susceptible to heat, resulting in a loss of flow rate. This can cause sudden loss of propulsion while driving. The fuel sensor housing may also crack and leak fuel, causing fuel starvation.
items.repairVsReplace: Fuel pump and FDM replacement is covered under recall for affected vehicles. For out‑of‑warranty vehicles, replacement costs £600-£1,200. Read our full /failures/fuel-pump-failure guide

items.title: Dipstick‑Tube Seal Oil Leaks
items.whatHappens: The rubber grommet where the dipstick tube enters the block hardens with heat cycles. Oil seeps out, leaving a mess on the block and exhaust manifold.
items.repairVsReplace: Seal replacement is a low‑cost repair (£50-£150) but should be addressed promptly to prevent oil loss and potential fire risk.

failures.goodYearsLine: The 55273835 2.0 GME has been in production since 2016. The engine is offered in multiple power outputs: 200 hp (147 kW) with 330 Nm torque, and 280 hp (206 kW) with 400 Nm torque. Later production engines (2020+) feature improved components and seem to have fewer reported issues. The 280 hp Veloce variant produces its peak power at 5,250 rpm, while the 200 hp variant peaks at 4,500 rpm. The engine meets various Euro 6 emissions standards including Euro 6d‑TEMP.

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the 55273835 2.0 GME
variants.intro: The 55273835 is a Specific engine code covering Alfa Romeo's 2.0‑litre turbocharged GME engine. Unlike Family pages that cover multiple fundamentally different engines, this page covers the 55273835 as a single engine with multiple output tunes. The engine is part of the FCA Global Medium Engine (GME) family and was developed specifically for the Giorgio platform. Where to find your engine code: The engine code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block and appears on the V5C registration document under "Engine number" - the code will read 55273835 followed by additional characters. Use an Alfa Romeo VIN decoder to confirm the exact variant from the build sheet. Key 55273835 variants: | Variant | Power | Torque | Key Difference | Applications | |---|---|---|---|---| | 55273835 (200 hp) | 200 hp (147 kW) @ 4,500 rpm | 330 Nm @ 1,750 rpm | Lower‑output tune, different ECU calibration | Giulia 2.0 Turbo 200 HP, Stelvio 2.0 Turbo 200 HP | | 55273835 (280 hp) | 280 hp (206 kW) @ 5,250 rpm | 400 Nm @ 2,250 rpm | Higher‑output tune, different turbo calibration | Giulia Veloce, Stelvio Veloce, Ti, Sprint | Why fitting the wrong variant matters: While both variants share the same basic architecture (1,995 cc, 84.0 mm bore × 90.0 mm stroke, 10.0:1 compression ratio), they have different ECU calibrations, turbocharger boost levels, and in some cases, different fuel injector specifications. Fitting a 200 hp ECU into a 280 hp vehicle will result in reduced performance and potential drivability issues. Commonly confused codes: | Engine Code | What it is | Why it's confused | |---|---|---| | 55273835 (FCA US Hurricane) | American‑market GME variant | Same family but different emissions hardware - not interchangeable |

relatives.description: the 1.75-litre turbo petrol that preceded the 2.0 GME in the Alfa Romeo Giulietta and 159. A 235 hp (175 kW) engine with a cast-iron block and aluminium head, the 1750 TBi was a characterful engine with a distinctive Alfa character. The 2.0 GME replaced it in the Giulia and Stelvio, offering more power (up to 280 hp) and better fuel economy.

the 2.2-litre naturally aspirated JTS (Jet Thrust Stoichiometric) engine used in the 159 and Brera. Producing 185 hp, the JTS was a direct-injection engine without turbocharging. The 2.0 GME is a significant improvement - more power, more torque, and better efficiency.

output 200 hp variant: The 200 hp (147 kW) tune of the 55273835, fitted to entry-level Giulia and Stelvio models. Shares the same hardware as the 280 hp variant but with different ECU calibration and lower boost pressure. Many owners consider remapping the 200 hp variant to 280 hp, though this requires specialist ECU tuning.

output 280 hp variant: The 280 hp (206 kW) tune of the 55273835, fitted to Giulia and Stelvio Veloce, Ti and Sprint models. Features the same core hardware as the 200 hp variant but with higher boost, different injector calibration, and a more aggressive ECU map. Produces 400 Nm torque at 2,250 rpm.

relatives.description: breathing 2.9-litre V6 used in the Giulia Quadrifoglio and Stelvio Quadrifoglio. Produces 503-510 hp. While sharing the Giorgio platform, the 2.9 V6 is a completely different engine - it's derived from Ferrari's V8 architecture and is not interchangeable with the 2.0 GME.

Rebuild costs (£5,000-£6,500+) are significant - only consider this for high‑value or sentimental vehicles. Link once:

items.question: What is the most common failure on the Alfa Romeo 55273835 2.0 GME?
items.answer: Timing chain stretch is the most critical issue, with many owners reporting symptoms as early as 40,000 miles - causing cold‑start rattle, rough idle, and Check Engine warnings. Left unaddressed, the chain can jump teeth and cause catastrophic engine failure. Carbon buildup on intake valves (requiring walnut‑blasting every 30,000-50,000 miles), fuel pump/fuel delivery module issues, and dipstick‑tube seal oil leaks are also common. Timing chain replacement costs £1,500-£3,000 at a specialist. Carbon cleaning costs £400-£800. Regular oil changes (5,000-9,000 miles) with the correct oil are critical. Many 2020+ models have improved timing chain components.

items.question: Is the 55273835 2.0 GME reliable, and what mileage can I expect?
items.answer: The 55273835 has an estimated lifespan of 100,000-150,000 miles with proper maintenance. The key to longevity is diligent oil changes (every 5,000-9,000 miles using the correct 0W‑30 or 5W‑30 oil) and early attention to timing chain warning signs. Many owners report 60,000+ trouble‑free miles with proactive maintenance. Budget for timing chain inspection around 40,000-60,000 miles. Carbon cleaning should be considered every 30,000-50,000 miles. The 2020+ models feature improved components and fewer reported issues. Regular Italian tune‑ups (spirited driving) can help keep carbon deposits at bay.
